item.content:encoded:
Scientific evidence is essential for solving many of the world’s most pressing challenges, from climate change and public health to technological innovation and sustainable development. However, producing quality scientific research is only part of the solution. Equally important is ensuring that scientific evidence is communicated effectively so that policymakers, governments, international organizations, and society can understand, trust, and act upon it. To strengthen this critical connection between science and policy, the International Science Council (ISC) has opened applications for its prestigious ISC Civic Science Fellow 2026. This fully funded, 18-month Fellowship provides an exceptional opportunity for outstanding early- to mid-career researchers who are passionate about science communication, public engagement, and evidence-informed policymaking. Hosted virtually by the International Science Council, the Fellowship enables researchers to work directly with one of the world’s leading science organizations while contributing to innovative research that improves the communication of scientific evidence in international policy processes.

The Fellowship is funded through the Rita Allen Civic Science Fellows Program, offering participants a monthly stipend of approximately USD 5,000, international networking opportunities, and the chance to influence how scientific evidence informs global decision-making.

About the International Science Council Civic Science Fellowship

The ISC Civic Science Fellowship is designed for researchers who want to bridge the gap between science and policymaking by improving how scientific evidence is communicated across complex international environments.

Today’s policy decisions are increasingly influenced by scientific research. Yet communicating scientific evidence effectively within multilateral institutions remains challenging due to political, institutional, social, and cultural factors that affect how information is interpreted and utilized.

This Fellowship addresses these challenges by enabling researchers to investigate communication strategies, develop practical tools, and strengthen the role of science in international governance.

Throughout the Fellowship, participants will work closely with:

  • The International Science Council Secretariat
  • Global scientific organizations
  • International partners
  • Communication professionals
  • Policymakers
  • Scientists
  • International organizations
  • Academic researchers

The goal is to identify and implement more effective ways of communicating scientific evidence to support better policymaking around the world.

Fellowship Overview

Fellowship Detail Information
Fellowship Duration 18 Months
Host Organization International Science Council (ISC)
Location Remote (Virtual)
Possible Travel Yes, including visits to Paris and selected UN locations
Start Date September 2026
Funding Fully Funded
Monthly Stipend Approximately USD 5,000
Funding Provider Rita Allen Civic Science Fellows Program
Application Deadline 16 August 2026

Why This Fellowship Matters

Scientific research alone does not automatically influence public policy.

Many global decisions are shaped by:

  • Political priorities
  • Institutional processes
  • Public trust
  • Communication quality
  • Cultural differences
  • Information ecosystems
  • Digital media environments
  • Public perception
  • Misinformation and disinformation

As a result, scientific evidence often struggles to reach decision-makers in ways that are understandable, trusted, and actionable. The ISC Civic Science Fellowship seeks to address these challenges by helping researchers understand how science can be communicated more effectively within international governance systems. Participants will contribute to real-world research while developing practical guidance that can improve science communication worldwide.

Fellowship Responsibilities

During the 18-month Fellowship, participants will contribute to a wide range of research and engagement activities.

These include:

1. Mapping Existing Science Communication Practices

The Fellow will:

  • Examine current communication approaches used by international organizations.
  • Study communication channels.
  • Analyze audience engagement strategies.
  • Identify effective communication models across different organizations.

2. Conducting Research on Scientific Information Ecosystems

Participants will investigate:

  • How scientific evidence is communicated.
  • How audiences interpret scientific information.
  • Factors influencing evidence uptake.
  • The role of institutional and political environments.

3. Identifying Barriers to Evidence-Based Decision-Making

Research activities include examining:

  • Obstacles preventing scientific evidence from influencing policy.
  • Institutional challenges.
  • Communication gaps.
  • Trust issues.
  • Cultural considerations.

4. Studying Digital Information Environments

The Fellow will analyze how evolving digital platforms influence science communication, including:

  • Misinformation
  • Disinformation
  • Digital media
  • Online engagement
  • Public information behavior

5. Applying Behavioural and Social Science

Participants will use evidence from:

  • Behavioural science
  • Psychology
  • Communication studies
  • Social sciences

to identify more effective approaches for communicating scientific evidence to diverse audiences.

6. Developing Practical Communication Resources

The Fellow will help create:

  • Communication toolkits
  • Practical guidance
  • Best practice documents
  • Evidence communication frameworks
  • Resources for scientific organizations

7. Testing New Communication Approaches

Working alongside ISC initiatives, the Fellow will:

  • Pilot communication strategies.
  • Evaluate their effectiveness.
  • Recommend improvements.

8. Producing Publications

Expected outputs include:

  • Research reports
  • Policy briefs
  • Analytical papers
  • Guidance documents
  • Publications for international audiences

9. Supporting International Networks

The Fellow will contribute to:

  • Academic engagement
  • Stakeholder outreach
  • International collaborations
  • Professional networking

Who Should Apply?

The Fellowship is particularly suited for researchers interested in:

  • Science communication
  • Public engagement with science
  • Trust in science
  • Behavioural science
  • Evidence-informed policymaking
  • Public policy
  • International governance
  • Civic science
  • Decision-making research
  • Information ecosystems

Applicants passionate about understanding how people engage with scientific evidence and how scientific knowledge shapes society are especially encouraged to apply.

Eligibility Requirements

Applicants must satisfy all of the following requirements:

  • Hold a PhD or expect to complete one before September 2026.
  • Be available full-time throughout the 18-month Fellowship.
  • Obtain employer support if currently employed.
  • Sign the required agreements with the ISC and the Rita Allen Foundation.
  • Possess a valid passport.
  • Be eligible for international travel and visas.
  • Participate in weekly Tuesday Learning Labs from noon to 2:00 pm ET.
  • Be available to begin the Fellowship in September 2026.

Desired Skills and Experience

Strong applicants should demonstrate:

  • Excellent research experience.
  • High-quality academic publications.
  • Expertise in science communication.
  • Experience working with governments or international organizations.
  • Ability to translate research into policy guidance.
  • Outstanding written and spoken English.
  • Strong communication and facilitation skills.
  • Ability to work independently in international environments.

Additional desirable experience includes:

  • International collaborations.
  • Interdisciplinary research.
  • Capacity-building initiatives.
  • Work within multilateral organizations.

Relevant Academic Fields

Researchers from a variety of disciplines are encouraged to apply, including:

  • Behavioural Science
  • Cognitive Science
  • Psychology
  • Science Communication
  • Political Science
  • Public Policy
  • Risk Analysis
  • Decision Science
  • Individual and Collective Action Research

Fellowship Benefits

Successful Fellows will receive numerous professional and financial benefits, including:

Financial Support

  • Fully funded Fellowship.
  • Monthly stipend of approximately USD 5,000.
  • Funding through the Rita Allen Civic Science Fellows Program.

Career Development

Participants will:

  • Conduct high-impact applied research.
  • Work with globally recognized scientific organizations.
  • Gain experience in international science policy.
  • Strengthen leadership skills.
  • Enhance science communication expertise.

International Exposure

Fellows will have opportunities to:

  • Collaborate with experts worldwide.
  • Participate in international meetings.
  • Attend workshops and conferences.
  • Visit the ISC headquarters in Paris.
  • Engage with United Nations-related activities.

Professional Networking

Participants will become part of an international network of:

  • Scientists
  • Science communicators
  • Policy experts
  • Journalists
  • Researchers
  • International organizations

Long-Term Impact

The Fellowship enables participants to contribute to global resources that improve science communication and evidence-informed policymaking for scientific organizations around the world.

Why You Should Apply

This Fellowship offers much more than financial support.

It provides an opportunity to:

  • Influence international science policy.
  • Work alongside globally recognized experts.
  • Build an international professional network.
  • Improve public understanding of science.
  • Help combat misinformation and disinformation.
  • Develop practical tools that support evidence-based policymaking.
  • Gain valuable experience working across science, communication, and governance.

For researchers passionate about making science more accessible and impactful, this Fellowship represents an exceptional career opportunity.

How to Apply

Interested candidates should complete the official online application form provided by the International Science Council HERE

Also, read more using same link. Applicants should ensure that all required documents are submitted before the application deadline and carefully review the eligibility criteria before applying.

Conclusion

The ISC Civic Science Fellow 2026 is an outstanding opportunity for early- to mid-career researchers seeking to shape the future of science communication and international policymaking. Through fully funded support, a generous monthly stipend, international collaboration, and direct engagement with leading scientific and policy organizations, Fellows will gain invaluable experience while contributing to the advancement of evidence-informed decision-making worldwide. If you have a passion for science communication, interdisciplinary research, and global policy engagement, this Fellowship offers a unique platform to develop your expertise, expand your international network, and make a lasting impact on how scientific evidence is communicated and used across the world. With applications closing on 16 August 2026, interested candidates should begin preparing their applications as early as possible

For more GLOBAL FELLOWSHIPS click HERE

item.content:encoded:
The United Nations System Staff College is accepting applications for two Associate Digital Learning Officer positions based in Turin, Italy. The roles are offered at the P2 level within the Digital Learning Services Unit of UNSSC’s Integrated Business Centre.

Under vacancy number VA/UNSSC/007/2026, the selected candidates will support the design, administration and continuous development of UNSSC’s digital learning ecosystem. The positions combine learning management system administration, instructional design, digital content management, user-experience research, stakeholder engagement and service-quality improvement.

The initial appointment will last for one year. Any extension will depend on satisfactory performance and the availability of funds.

Applications must be submitted by 24 August 2026.

About the United Nations System Staff College

The United Nations System Staff College provides learning and knowledge services to personnel across the United Nations system and its partner organisations.

UNSSC develops learning experiences grounded in the principles of multilateralism, human dignity and the values of the United Nations Charter. Its programmes help participants strengthen their knowledge and professional capabilities in areas including:

  • Leadership and management
  • Sustainable development
  • Peace and security
  • Organisational learning
  • Digital learning and knowledge exchange

UNSSC is headquartered in Turin, Italy, and also operates an office in Bonn, Germany.

Its work is organised through two connected departments:

  1. Learning and Knowledge Services
  2. Integrated Business Centre

The Integrated Business Centre supports UNSSC’s Directorate and programmes by improving service quality, strengthening compliance with United Nations rules, identifying business opportunities and applying innovative technologies to increase efficiency and institutional impact.

About the Digital Learning Services Unit

The two positions are located in the Digital Learning Services Unit within the Integrated Business Centre.

The unit manages important parts of UNSSC’s digital learning infrastructure, including:

  • The UNSSC Learning Management System
  • The Blue Line global learning hub
  • Digital content portfolios
  • Learning pathways
  • User support services
  • Platform development and quality assurance
  • Learning analytics and user-experience research

The Blue Line is designed as a global platform for personalised and self-directed learning. The Digital Learning Services Unit also oversees the administration and continued development of UNSSC’s Learning Management System.

UNSSC treats technical platform administration, content management and learning-experience design as closely connected areas. The Associate Digital Learning Officers will therefore work across all three areas rather than focusing exclusively on technical support or course design.

Main Purpose of the Positions

The selected officers will work at the intersection of:

  • Learning technology
  • Instructional design
  • Content architecture
  • User experience
  • Client support
  • Digital service development

They will help UNSSC maintain a coherent, high-quality and continuously improving digital learning offer for United Nations personnel and partner organisations.

Both officers will report directly to the Team Lead of the Integrated Business Centre’s Digital Learning Services Unit.

Learning Management System Responsibilities

A significant part of the role involves the administration and development of UNSSC’s Learning Management System.

The selected candidates will support daily LMS operations, including:

  • Creating and managing user accounts
  • Assigning roles and permissions
  • Processing enrolments
  • Setting up courses
  • Maintaining accurate platform records
  • Applying established governance policies

They will also provide technical assistance through the LMS Service Desk. This includes responding to user requests, resolving problems within agreed service timelines and maintaining support materials such as:

  • User guides
  • Frequently asked questions
  • Standard operating procedures
  • Administrative instructions
  • Troubleshooting resources

The officers will advise clients on how to structure and configure courses within the LMS. This guidance may cover content organisation, assessment design, learner pathways and the use of platform functions to improve learning effectiveness.

LMS Development and Quality Assurance

The successful candidates will contribute to the development and testing of new LMS features and system improvements.

Their responsibilities may include:

  1. Helping define requirements for new platform functions
  2. Preparing technical specifications and user stories
  3. Coordinating with external vendors
  4. Testing new functionalities
  5. Confirming that technical outputs meet agreed requirements
  6. Identifying defects or configuration problems before deployment
  7. Supporting the release of approved enhancements

The officers will also support UNSSC’s ISO 9001:2015 Quality Management System as it relates to LMS operations.

This may involve documenting service processes, maintaining operational controls, recording non-conformities, preparing for internal audits and monitoring indicators related to service quality and customer satisfaction.

Blue Line Content Architecture

The officers will help coordinate the Blue Line content portfolio and maintain its content-architecture framework.

This work includes supporting:

  • Taxonomy structures
  • Content categories
  • Audience segmentation
  • Learning-pathway logic
  • Publication standards
  • Content-review processes
  • Periodic content updates

They will coordinate with UNSSC programme teams, external contributors and subject-matter experts throughout the full content lifecycle.

This process may begin with the initial content concept and continue through development, instructional review, publication, monitoring and eventual revision.

Instructional Design and Content Development

Applicants should be comfortable applying instructional-design principles to digital content.

The selected officers will contribute to the development of Blue Line learning materials and advise internal and external content creators on issues such as:

  • Formulating learning objectives
  • Structuring learning content
  • Designing assessments
  • Building learner pathways
  • Encouraging learner engagement
  • Applying learner-centred approaches
  • Maintaining consistent instructional quality

They will help ensure that content meets UNSSC standards regardless of whether it was developed internally or submitted by another United Nations entity or partner organisation.

The officers will also act as an operational link between Digital Learning Services and the Learning and Knowledge Services department. This will involve coordinating planning activities, shared content-review cycles and cross-functional development initiatives.

User-Experience and Accessibility Reviews

The officers will conduct periodic quality reviews of Blue Line courses, learning pathways and related platform activities.

Reviews may examine:

  • Course configuration
  • Accuracy of course descriptions
  • Content consistency
  • Accessibility
  • Navigation
  • Learner engagement
  • Alignment with instructional standards
  • Appropriate use of platform functions

Where problems are identified, the officers will coordinate the necessary corrections.

They will also help map user touchpoints across the learner journey and identify areas where participants experience confusion, delay or unnecessary difficulty.

Blue Line Live Events and Communities of Practice

The selected candidates will help organise Blue Line Live events.

Their responsibilities may include:

  • Developing event concepts
  • Coordinating speakers
  • Promoting sessions
  • Supporting facilitation
  • Managing event logistics
  • Conducting post-event follow-up

Live events should complement the platform’s self-directed learning resources rather than operate as disconnected activities.

The officers will also support the development of a community-of-practice model for Blue Line. They may assist existing United Nations communities and onboard new ones by providing orientation, facilitation guidance and resources that help maintain participation and generate useful content.

Monitoring, Analytics and User Research

The positions require the ability to use operational and user data to improve digital services.

The officers will monitor information such as:

  • Platform usage
  • Learner engagement
  • Satisfaction survey results
  • User feedback
  • Adoption trends
  • Service performance
  • Client-support patterns

They will help prepare interview guides, surveys and other research instruments. Findings from user research and monitoring will then be translated into practical recommendations, technical requirements or service improvements.

The officers will be expected to ensure that user feedback is systematically incorporated into improvement cycles across both the LMS and Blue Line.

Communication and Stakeholder Engagement

The roles also involve communication, outreach and capacity development.

The successful candidates may prepare:

  • Newsletters
  • Platform announcements
  • Contributor guidance
  • User-facing documentation
  • Training materials
  • Adoption and engagement reports
  • Digital outreach content

They will support onboarding and training activities for new LMS administrators, course owners and Blue Line contributors.

Clear language, strong communication and the ability to adapt information to different audiences will be essential.

Required Education

Applicants must hold an advanced university degree in a relevant field, such as:

  • Adult learning
  • Instructional design
  • Digital marketing
  • Cognitive science
  • Social sciences
  • Related human sciences

A first-level university degree may be accepted instead of an advanced degree where the applicant has an appropriate combination of academic qualifications and relevant professional experience.

Required Professional Experience

Applicants must have at least two years of professional experience in one or more of the following areas:

  • LMS administration
  • Instructional design
  • Digital content management
  • Digital learning
  • Related learning-technology functions

Candidates must demonstrate experience in course design and development, including writing learning objectives, structuring content and designing assessments.

They must also have experience advising content authors, course administrators or subject-matter experts on course setup, learner pathways and engagement strategies within an LMS environment.

Additional required experience includes:

  • Configuring and administering LMS platforms
  • Publishing and quality-assuring digital learning content
  • Analysing user feedback or satisfaction data
  • Working with user-experience research outputs
  • Coordinating multi-stakeholder content-development processes
  • Managing editorial reviews and content lifecycles

Experience with Moodle or a comparable enterprise LMS is particularly relevant.

Desirable Experience

The following experience is considered advantageous:

  • Supporting ISO 9001:2015 or a similar quality-management framework
  • Developing engagement strategies for digital services
  • Promoting learning-platform adoption
  • Working within the United Nations system
  • Using enterprise resource-planning systems
  • Working with Drupal or a similar content-management system
  • Using Salesforce or another customer-relationship-management platform
  • Applying UX research and measurement methods

Previous United Nations experience is highly desirable but is not listed as a mandatory requirement.

Language Requirements

Fluency in spoken and written English is required.

Knowledge of another official United Nations language is desirable.

Required Competencies

UNSSC is seeking candidates who demonstrate:

  • Professionalism
  • Planning and organisational ability
  • Client orientation
  • Clear communication
  • Creativity
  • Teamwork
  • Commitment to continuous learning
  • Technological awareness

Applicants should be able to manage several operational workstreams, meet service standards, communicate effectively with clients and translate technical or learning-related challenges into practical solutions.

How to Apply

Applications must be submitted in English and include:

  1. A completed, updated and signed United Nations P11 form
  2. A concise motivation letter explaining why the applicant is qualified
  3. Submission through the official UNSSC online application form

Candidates should apply through the employment opportunities section of the UNSSC website.

Applicants with disabilities may request reasonable accommodation to support their participation in the recruitment process. Any request should be indicated in the application.

APPLY HERE

Application Deadline

The deadline for applications is:

24 August 2026

The vacancy announcement does not specify a closing time or time zone. Candidates should submit their applications before the final day to reduce the risk of technical difficulties.

Conclusion

The UNSSC Associate Digital Learning Officer positions offer an opportunity for professionals with experience in learning technologies, instructional design and digital content management to contribute to the United Nations learning ecosystem.

The two selected officers will support LMS administration, Blue Line content development, platform quality assurance, user research, stakeholder engagement and continuous service improvement.

Applicants should demonstrate both technical competence and an understanding of how digital platforms can create effective, accessible and learner-centred experiences.

The positions are based in Turin, Italy, at the P2 level, with an initial duration of one year. Applications must be submitted by 24 August 2026.

For more information about this opportunity and the application process, CLICK HERE.

To discover more job opportunities, VISIT HERE.

item.content:encoded:
The AEIP Scholars Programme 2026–2027 is now accepting applications from outstanding young researchers across Africa and Europe who are passionate about advancing research, innovation, and international collaboration. The programme offers an exceptional opportunity for emerging scholars to work across continents, co-create practical research solutions, strengthen academic partnerships, and contribute to addressing some of the world’s most pressing shared challenges.

Launched by the Africa-Europe Innovation Platform (AEIP), the Scholars Programme is a collaborative research initiative designed to foster stronger scientific cooperation between Africa and Europe. Through peer learning, joint research, innovation, and science communication, the programme empowers scholars to translate academic research into practical solutions that create meaningful impact for communities, institutions, women, and youth.

Successful applicants will become part of a highly selective international cohort and collaborate directly with scholars from another continent while receiving the opportunity to showcase their research at the prestigious AEIP Stakeholder Meeting in Europe in June 2027.

Applications are currently open and will close on 31 August 2026.

What is the AEIP Scholars Programme?

The AEIP Scholars Programme is a collaborative research impact programme that connects emerging scholars from Africa and Europe to encourage interdisciplinary research and strengthen long-term cooperation between both regions.

Rather than conducting research independently, selected participants will be paired with scholars from another continent to jointly develop innovative, solution-driven research outputs based on their existing work.

The programme focuses on transforming academic knowledge into practical innovations capable of addressing shared challenges facing both Africa and Europe.

It also encourages scholars to expand their international networks while developing skills in:

  • Collaborative research
  • Research impact
  • Innovation
  • Science communication
  • International partnership building
  • Knowledge exchange
  • Cross-cultural academic collaboration

Programme Objectives

The AEIP Scholars Programme seeks to strengthen collaboration between African and European researchers by supporting research that aligns with the AU-EU Innovation Agenda, particularly its Capacities for Science Action.

The programme aims to:

  • Foster collaborative research between Africa and Europe
  • Encourage innovation through interdisciplinary partnerships
  • Promote knowledge exchange between scholars
  • Strengthen long-term academic cooperation
  • Support practical research addressing global challenges
  • Develop innovative solutions with measurable societal impact
  • Increase science communication capacity
  • Build stronger international research networks

Understanding the AU-EU Innovation Agenda

The Scholars Programme is built around the Capacities for Science Action under the AU-EU Innovation Agenda.

This initiative seeks to strengthen scientific cooperation by supporting:

  • Collaboration between African and European universities
  • Partnerships among research institutions
  • Joint innovation activities
  • Academic exchange programmes
  • Knowledge transfer initiatives
  • Learning mobility opportunities
  • Research collaborations addressing socioeconomic challenges
  • Joint training programmes
  • Recognition of higher education qualifications
  • Academic and professional mobility
  • Curriculum development
  • Capacity building for students, researchers and postdoctoral fellows
  • Digital education systems
  • Digital transformation
  • Digital skills development
  • Youth employability
  • Reducing talent drain
  • Inclusive innovation ecosystems

Through the Scholars Programme, participants contribute directly to these international objectives.

How the Programme Works

The programme follows a structured collaborative model.

Step 1: Selection

A total of 10 scholars will be selected.

Participants will come from both:

  • Africa
  • Europe

Step 2: Scholar Pairing

Each scholar will be paired with another participant from the opposite continent.

This creates:

  • Five Africa-Europe research pairs

Pairing is based on:

  • Shared research interests
  • Complementary expertise
  • Similar academic themes

Step 3: Collaborative Research

Each Africa-Europe scholar pair will work together to:

  • Develop a collaborative research activity
  • Produce a joint research output
  • Design a practical innovation based on their research

The emphasis is on creating research that delivers real-world solutions rather than remaining purely theoretical.

Step 4: Expert Evaluation

The completed research outputs will be evaluated by an expert panel.

Projects will be reviewed according to several criteria, including:

  • Innovation
  • Practicality
  • Scalability
  • Social impact
  • Research quality

Step 5: Final Pitching Event

The top-performing scholar pairs will present their research solutions through a competitive pitching process.

The three highest-ranked teams will become finalists.

Step 6: AEIP Stakeholder Meeting

Finalist teams will receive sponsorship to attend the AEIP Stakeholder Meeting in Europe in June 2027, where they will showcase their collaborative research to stakeholders, experts, and innovation leaders.

Evaluation Criteria

Applications submitted during the selection stage will be assessed based on:

  • Relevance of the research
  • Academic excellence
  • Innovation potential
  • Alignment with Africa-Europe cooperation priorities

During the collaborative phase, proposed solutions will be evaluated according to:

  • Impact on women and youth
  • Ability to strengthen communities and institutions
  • Strength of the proposed solution
  • Technology-driven innovation
  • Practical feasibility
  • Realistic implementation potential

Expected Programme Outcomes

The AEIP Scholars Programme aims to generate long-term impact by producing:

  • Collaborative Africa-Europe research outputs
  • Innovative practical solutions
  • Stronger international academic partnerships
  • Enhanced research capacity
  • Improved knowledge exchange
  • Sustainable development initiatives
  • Inclusive innovation ecosystems
  • Cross-border scientific collaboration

Benefits of the AEIP Scholars Programme

Selected scholars will enjoy numerous academic and professional benefits, including:

  • Opportunity to collaborate internationally with leading young researchers
  • Cross-continental research partnerships
  • Peer learning opportunities
  • Enhanced research visibility
  • International networking
  • Innovation development experience
  • Science communication skills
  • Exposure to expert reviewers
  • Opportunity to present research before international stakeholders
  • Sponsored participation at the AEIP Stakeholder Meeting in Europe (for finalist teams)
  • Increased career development opportunities
  • Contribution to solving shared global challenges

Who Can Apply?

The programme welcomes applications from young scholars who satisfy all eligibility requirements.

Applicants must:

  • Be between 25 and 35 years old
  • Be based in Africa or Europe
  • Be enrolled in a PhD, Postdoctoral programme, or further studies during the application period
  • Have ongoing or completed:
    • Research projects
    • Theses
    • Dissertations

Their research must align with the AU-EU Innovation Agenda Capacities for Science Action.

Application Requirements

Interested applicants must submit an Expression of Interest that includes an abstract of their research.

The submitted abstract should demonstrate:

  • Research relevance
  • Academic quality
  • Innovation
  • Potential impact
  • Alignment with Africa-Europe priorities

Programme Timeline

July – August 2026

  • Applications open
  • Programme officially launched

31 August 2026

  • Application deadline

September 2026

  • Selection of 10 scholars
  • Africa-Europe scholar pairing

September 2026 – March 2027

  • Collaborative research period
  • Development of joint research outputs

First Half of April 2027

  • Evaluation of submitted projects
  • Selection of the top three scholar pairs

June 2027

  • AEIP Stakeholder Meeting in Europe
  • Final presentations by the top three scholar pairs

How to Apply

Eligible applicants should submit their Expression of Interest through the official Africa-Europe Innovation Platform application process before the application deadline.

Applicants are encouraged to carefully prepare a strong research abstract that clearly demonstrates:

  • Originality
  • Research excellence
  • Practical relevance
  • Innovation potential
  • Alignment with the AU-EU Innovation Agenda

Early applications are strongly recommended.

APPLY NOW

Need Assistance?

For programme enquiries, applicants may contact:

Email: info@africaeuropeinnovation.net

When contacting the organisers, include “Scholars Programme” in the subject line.

Application Deadline

31 August 2026

Late applications are unlikely to be considered. Interested scholars are encouraged to submit their Expression of Interest well before the deadline.

Conclusion

The AEIP Scholars Programme 2026–2027 offers an outstanding opportunity for emerging researchers from Africa and Europe to collaborate across borders, transform academic research into practical solutions, and strengthen international scientific partnerships. By combining innovation, knowledge exchange, and interdisciplinary collaboration, the programme prepares the next generation of scholars to address global challenges while expanding their academic and professional networks.

For young researchers seeking international exposure, collaborative research experience, and the opportunity to contribute to meaningful innovation, the AEIP Scholars Programme represents an excellent platform for growth. Eligible scholars are encouraged to prepare their strongest research abstracts and submit their applications before 31 August 2026.

item.content:encoded:
Applications are open for the Dorothy and Lewis B. Cullman Center Fellowship 2027–2028, a prestigious international residential programme offered by The New York Public Library for outstanding scholars, journalists, translators, creative writers and selected visual artists.

Each year, the Cullman Center appoints 15 Fellows for a nine-month term running from September through May. The programme is intended for applicants whose proposed work will benefit directly from access to the extensive research collections housed at the Stephen A. Schwarzman Building in New York City.

Selected Fellows receive a $90,000 stipend, a private office equipped with a computer and full access to the Library’s physical and electronic resources. Fellows are also welcomed into an interdisciplinary community where scholarly research and creative work meet across the long oak tables of one of the world’s great libraries.

The application deadline for the 2027–2028 fellowship cycle is Friday, September 25, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. EDT.

About the Dorothy and Lewis B. Cullman Center

The Dorothy and Lewis B. Cullman Center for Scholars and Writers is located at The New York Public Library’s landmark Stephen A. Schwarzman Building at Fifth Avenue and 42nd Street in Manhattan.

Established in 1999, the Center provides dedicated space for sustained research and writing while giving Fellows enhanced access to the Library’s internationally renowned collections. It brings together outstanding academic and creative thinkers from the United States and other countries and supports the development of new books, scholarship and literary work.

The programme is designed around two complementary forms of work:

  • The concentrated, often solitary process of research and writing
  • The collaborative exchange of ideas among Fellows and through public Library programmes

The Cullman Center therefore offers both privacy and intellectual community. Fellows pursue their individual projects while regularly discussing their work with scholars and writers from different disciplines and creative traditions.

Purpose of the Cullman Center Fellowship

The fellowship provides talented writers and researchers with the time, resources and institutional setting required to complete ambitious projects.

Its central purpose is to support work that depends meaningfully on the collections of the Stephen A. Schwarzman Building.

Applicants should not treat access to the Library as a decorative feature of their proposal. They must be able to explain why specific collections, archives, languages, materials or research divisions are important to the proposed project.

The Library’s research strengths include:

  • Anthropology
  • Art
  • Geography
  • History
  • Languages and literature
  • Philosophy
  • Politics
  • Popular culture
  • Psychology
  • Religion
  • Sociology
  • Sports
  • Urban studies

The Schwarzman Building is recognised as a major international research resource across these and related fields.

Fellowship Duration and Location

The Cullman Center Fellowship lasts for nine months, from September through May.

For the 2027–2028 cycle, Fellows will carry out their work primarily at:

The Dorothy and Lewis B. Cullman Center for Scholars and Writers
Stephen A. Schwarzman Building
The New York Public Library
Fifth Avenue and 42nd Street
New York City

Fellows are expected to work at the Cullman Center five days a week, Monday through Friday, for the duration of the fellowship term.

Applicants should therefore be prepared to make the programme their main professional commitment during the fellowship period.

Financial Support and Fellowship Benefits

Each selected Cullman Center Fellow receives the following support.

$90,000 Stipend

The fellowship provides a stipend of $90,000 for the nine-month term.

Applicants should review the official fellowship and appointment documents for any applicable payment schedule, tax or administrative conditions.

Private Office

Every Fellow receives the use of a private office with a computer at the Cullman Center.

This provides a dedicated environment for sustained research, writing and project development.

Full Library Access

Fellows receive full access to the Library’s physical and electronic research resources.

This may include:

  • Books and periodicals
  • Manuscripts
  • Archival collections
  • Maps
  • Photographs
  • Visual materials
  • Historical documents
  • Electronic databases
  • Specialist research collections
  • Support from curatorial and reference staff

Interdisciplinary Community

Fellows join a cohort of academics, writers, journalists, translators, independent scholars and artists.

The programme encourages discussion across fields that are often separated within universities or professional institutions.

Intellectual Exchange

Fellows participate in ongoing conversations within the Center and may contribute to public programmes across The New York Public Library.

The Center’s brochure notes that Fellows collaborate through weekly lunches and other opportunities to share their work.

Who Can Apply?

The Cullman Center Fellowship welcomes a broad range of scholarly and creative applicants.

Eligible applicants include:

  • Academics
  • Independent scholars
  • Journalists
  • Novelists
  • Playwrights
  • Poets
  • Translators
  • Nonfiction writers
  • Visual artists working on a book project

The defining requirement is not a particular job title. Instead, applicants must demonstrate that their project requires sustained access to the research collections at the Stephen A. Schwarzman Building.

The programme is international. Foreign nationals who are sufficiently proficient in English to participate in the fellowship community are welcome to apply.

Eligible Projects

Competitive projects are likely to combine high-quality writing, intellectual or creative originality and a clear need for the Library’s collections.

Projects may include:

  • Scholarly monographs
  • Historical studies
  • Literary nonfiction
  • Biographies
  • Novels
  • Poetry collections
  • Plays
  • Works of translation
  • Journalism and long-form reporting
  • Artist books
  • Visual projects being developed specifically as books

The fellowship is centred on substantial research and writing projects rather than general professional development.

Who Is Not Eligible?

Applicants seeking support for research that leads directly to a degree are not eligible.

This means the fellowship is not intended to fund:

  • Doctoral dissertations
  • Master’s theses
  • Degree-required research
  • Other projects whose direct purpose is completion of an academic qualification

Graduate students may therefore be ineligible where the proposed project forms part of their degree requirements.

Applicants who have completed their degrees and are developing independent post-degree projects may be considered if they meet the fellowship’s other requirements.

Selection Criteria

The Selection Committee awards 15 fellowships each year to outstanding scholars and writers.

The programme places strong emphasis on:

Quality of Writing

The Cullman Center seeks applicants who demonstrate writing of the highest quality.

This applies to both scholarly and creative applicants. A strong idea can stumble if presented through foggy prose; the committee is looking for both intellectual substance and command of language.

Strength of the Proposed Project

The project should be original, focused and achievable during the nine-month fellowship period.

Need for NYPL Collections

Applicants must show how the Library’s collections will contribute directly to the work.

A proposal should identify relevant materials or research areas rather than merely stating that the Library is useful.

Potential Contribution

The Center aims to promote dynamic communication about literature, scholarship and creative work through:

  • Exchange among Fellows
  • Public discussions
  • Programmes at the Library
  • Published work developed during or after the fellowship

Ability to Participate in the Community

Fellows should be prepared to engage constructively with colleagues working across different fields and forms of writing.

Fellowship Responsibilities

The fellowship provides significant time and resources, but it also comes with clear expectations.

Selected Fellows must:

  • Work primarily at the Cullman Center
  • Attend regularly from Monday through Friday
  • Pursue the project described in their application
  • Participate in the Center’s intellectual community
  • Present their current work to other Fellows and invited guests
  • Potentially participate in additional New York Public Library programmes

Each Fellow gives a lunchtime presentation on their work in progress.

These presentations create opportunities for critique, discussion and connections among researchers and writers who may approach knowledge from very different angles.

Public Programmes and Knowledge Exchange

The Cullman Center supports public conversations featuring current and former Fellows.

These programmes allow Fellows to discuss books and projects developed through the fellowship while connecting their research with wider audiences.

The Center’s public work reflects the Library’s broader mission of advancing knowledge, curiosity and the free exchange of ideas. Its brochure describes the programme as a forum for both individual research and the creation of new knowledge through public and interdisciplinary exchange.

Joint NYPL–ACLS Fellowships

The Cullman Center may award up to five fellowships each year in conjunction with the American Council of Learned Societies.

Applicants seeking a joint NYPL–ACLS Fellowship must submit:

  1. A separate application to The New York Public Library
  2. A separate application to the American Council of Learned Societies

Submitting one application does not automatically count as applying to both organisations.

The deadlines are also different:

  • ACLS application deadline: September 17, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. EDT
  • Cullman Center application deadline: September 25, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. EDT

Applicants interested in the joint opportunity should prepare for the earlier ACLS deadline.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

A strong application should make a convincing connection among the applicant, the proposed project and the Library’s collections.

Applicants should consider the following steps.

1. Define the Project Clearly

Explain the central subject, question or creative objective.

The committee should be able to understand what the applicant intends to produce and why it matters.

2. Identify Relevant Collections

Research the holdings of the Stephen A. Schwarzman Building before applying.

Name the archives, divisions, materials or subject collections that will be essential to the project.

3. Explain Why Residence Is Necessary

Describe why sustained work at the Library is important and what could be accomplished during the nine-month term.

4. Present an Achievable Plan

The proposal should be ambitious but realistic.

Applicants should explain the project’s current stage and the progress they expect to make during the fellowship.

5. Demonstrate Writing Excellence

Application materials and writing samples should be carefully edited, coherent and representative of the applicant’s strongest work.

6. Show Readiness for Interdisciplinary Exchange

Applicants should demonstrate an ability to communicate their work to people outside their immediate field.

How to Apply

Applicants must complete the official 2027–2028 Cullman Center Fellowship application through The New York Public Library.

Before submitting, candidates should review:

  • The fellowship scope
  • Selection criteria
  • Residency expectations
  • Application instructions
  • Required supporting materials
  • Policies concerning foreign applicants
  • Joint NYPL–ACLS application procedures, where relevant

APPLY HERE

Application Deadline

The deadline for the 2027–2028 Cullman Center Fellowship is:

Friday, September 25, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. EDT

Applicants pursuing the joint NYPL–ACLS Fellowship must submit the separate ACLS application by:

September 17, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. EDT

Because the deadlines include an exact time and time zone, international applicants should convert them carefully and submit early.

Conclusion

The Dorothy and Lewis B. Cullman Center Fellowship 2027–2028 offers an exceptional opportunity for scholars and writers whose projects depend on sustained engagement with The New York Public Library’s research collections.

Fifteen Fellows will receive a $90,000 stipend, a private office, full access to the Library’s resources and nine months of protected time for research and writing.

The fellowship welcomes academics, independent scholars, journalists, translators, creative writers and visual artists working on book projects. Applicants from outside the United States are welcome, provided they can participate effectively in English and meet the programme requirements.

The strongest applications will combine excellent writing, an ambitious but achievable project and a precise explanation of why the Schwarzman Building’s collections are indispensable.

Applications must be submitted by September 25, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. EDT.

For more information about this opportunity and the application process, CLICK HERE.

To discover more fellowship opportunities, VISIT HERE.

item.content:encoded:
The 2027 France-South Africa Scholarship Programme is officially open for applications, offering an exceptional opportunity for eligible students from South Africa, Lesotho, and Malawi to pursue Master’s and PhD degrees in France. This prestigious scholarship programme supports talented students who wish to undertake postgraduate studies at French universities and higher education institutions beginning in September 2027.

The initiative strengthens academic cooperation between France and Southern African countries while promoting research, innovation, international collaboration, and the development of highly skilled professionals across numerous disciplines. Students interested in obtaining world-class education in France are encouraged to submit their applications before the closing date.

Applications are currently open and must be submitted no later than 8 October 2026 at 23:59 (South Africa Time).

About the France-South Africa Scholarship Programme

The France-South Africa Scholarship Programme is designed to provide deserving students with an opportunity to pursue postgraduate studies in France. The programme specifically targets students who intend to enroll in accredited French universities or higher education institutions for either a Master’s degree or a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD).

The scholarship is part of France’s broader commitment to strengthening educational partnerships with African countries while supporting academic excellence, research collaboration, innovation, and capacity building.

Successful applicants will commence their studies in September 2027, following participation in preparatory online French language courses.

Why Study in France?

France remains one of the world’s leading destinations for higher education because of its:

  • Internationally recognized universities
  • Excellent research facilities
  • Strong academic reputation
  • Affordable higher education compared to many Western countries
  • Rich cultural heritage
  • Diverse international student community
  • Strong links between universities and industry
  • Opportunities for innovation and entrepreneurship

Studying in France also enables students to gain international exposure while building valuable professional and academic networks.

Who Can Apply?

The scholarship programme is open exclusively to applicants who hold citizenship of:

  • South Africa
  • Lesotho
  • Malawi

Applicants must intend to begin their postgraduate studies in France in September 2027.

Available Degree Levels

Applicants may apply to pursue:

  • Master’s Degree
  • PhD (Doctoral Degree)

The programme supports studies at recognized French universities and higher education institutions.

Fields of Study

Applications are accepted from all academic disciplines.

However, priority consideration will be given to applicants pursuing programmes in:

  • Science
  • Technology
  • Engineering
  • Mathematics (STEM)

The programme also recognizes related fields within:

  • Humanities
  • Social Sciences

This means applicants from non-STEM disciplines remain eligible to apply, although STEM-related applications may receive additional consideration during the selection process.

French Language Preparation

Because academic calendars differ between Southern Hemisphere countries and France, scholarship recipients will participate in online French language courses before travelling.

Successful applicants will receive:

  • Online French language training
  • Courses delivered by the Alliances Françaises network
  • Training period from February to July 2027

These courses are intended to help students integrate academically and socially before arriving in France.

Benefits of the Scholarship

While the announcement does not specify financial details, the programme offers successful applicants the opportunity to:

  • Study at prestigious French universities
  • Access internationally recognized postgraduate education
  • Receive French language preparation before departure
  • Join international academic and research communities
  • Build global professional networks
  • Enhance research and career prospects
  • Experience French culture and higher education

Applicants should consult the official programme rulebook for detailed scholarship benefits and funding information.

Important Resources for Applicants

Applicants are strongly encouraged to review the following resources before submitting their applications:

  • France-South Africa Scholarship Programme Rulebook
  • Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
  • Campus France South Africa website
  • Information about French universities
  • Available study programmes
  • Admission guidance

Students who require assistance selecting an appropriate programme are encouraged to contact Campus France South Africa for academic advice.

Selection Process

The scholarship selection process follows several stages:

  1. Submission of applications
  2. Eligibility review
  3. Interviews for shortlisted candidates
  4. Final selection
  5. Announcement of successful candidates
  6. French language preparation
  7. Departure to France

Applicants selected for interviews will be contacted individually.

Important Timeline

Applications Open

21 July 2026

Application Deadline

8 October 2026 at 23:59 (South Africa Time)

Information Webinar

August 2026

Applicants should follow Campus France South Africa’s social media platforms for webinar details.

Interviews

November 2026

Eligible candidates will be invited for interviews.

Announcement of Shortlisted Candidates

Beginning of December 2026

French Language Training

February – July 2027

Online language preparation through Alliances Françaises.

Departure to France

September 2027

Successful candidates begin their postgraduate studies in France.

Important Notes for Applicants

Applicants should keep the following in mind:

  • Read the scholarship rulebook carefully before applying.
  • Ensure all required documents are submitted before the deadline.
  • Late applications are unlikely to be accepted.
  • Scholarship recipients and shortlisted candidates will be contacted individually.
  • Due to the high volume of applications, follow-up inquiries from applicants will not receive responses.
  • If you have not received any communication from the scholarship panel by February 2027, you should consider your application unsuccessful.
  • Decisions made by the Scholarship Panel are final and cannot be appealed.

Tips for Preparing a Strong Application

To maximize your chances of success:

  • Begin your application early.
  • Carefully research suitable universities and programmes in France.
  • Prepare a compelling motivation letter.
  • Ensure your academic records are complete and accurate.
  • Clearly explain how your proposed studies align with your academic and career goals.
  • Verify that all supporting documents meet programme requirements.
  • Submit your application well before the deadline to avoid technical issues.

APPLY HERE

Why You Should Apply

The France-South Africa Scholarship Programme provides an outstanding opportunity for ambitious students seeking internationally recognized postgraduate education in France. Beyond earning a prestigious Master’s or PhD degree, recipients gain access to world-class research environments, international collaborations, cultural exchange, and valuable language training that prepares them for academic success.

Whether your ambitions lie in scientific research, technological innovation, engineering, social sciences, or the humanities, this scholarship offers a pathway toward advanced education and global career opportunities.

Students who meet the eligibility requirements are encouraged to begin preparing their applications as early as possible to ensure they submit a complete and competitive application before the deadline.

Visit HERE to learn more about the France-South Africa Scholarship Programme 2027

Conclusion

The France-South Africa Scholarship Programme 2027 represents a significant opportunity for talented postgraduate students from South Africa, Lesotho, and Malawi to pursue advanced studies in France. By supporting Master’s and PhD candidates across a broad range of disciplines, the programme promotes academic excellence, international collaboration, and long-term professional development.

Prospective applicants should carefully review all programme guidelines, research suitable institutions and study programmes, and submit complete applications before 8 October 2026 at 23:59 (South Africa Time). Early preparation, attention to detail, and a strong academic profile will significantly improve the likelihood of success.
